fields.meta_description: Build an interest form that counts replies by answer and emails the right people when your class or program gets the go-ahead.
fields.h1: Build an Interest Form That Counts Demand Before You Commit
fields.hero_description: Build an interest form that tallies demand for each option and alerts you when one reaches your go-ahead number.
fields.features_heading: What Turns Replies Into a Decision
fields.features_subheading: A spreadsheet of names tells you people are curious. These six pieces tell you what to schedule and when.
fields.feature_1:
Questions that change with each answer

Show the skill-level question only to people who pick the beginner course, and the position list only to players. Each person sees what applies to them and skips the rest.
fields.feature_2:
A running count for every option

Count replies per option as they arrive, by weeknight for a class or by age group for a league. Totals sit on a dashboard beside the raw rows, with no pivot table to rebuild.
fields.feature_3:
An alert when demand clears your bar

Set the number that makes something worth running, such as 8 people for a weekend class. When an option reaches it, the app sends a Slack or email note to the person who decides.
fields.feature_4:
Launch emails matched to each answer

Write the announcement once and send it only to people whose answers match, like everyone who chose a two-bedroom plan. Nobody gets news about an option they never picked.
fields.feature_5:
One row per person, updated in place

Match a returning person by email and update their row when they change an answer. Totals count people, not submissions, and someone who edits an answer never shows up twice.
fields.feature_6:
The whole app in your GitHub repo

Export the full code for the form and its dashboard to your GitHub on paid plans, follow-up emails included. Host the app wherever you like, or keep changing it in Emergent.
fields.why_title: Why Build Interest Forms With Emergent?
fields.why_description: A template collects names and stops there. Someone still copies replies into a sheet and tallies them by hand.

fields.tab_content_1:
Tuesday wins with 14 of 23 replies

Fernhill Community College has a woodshop that sits empty most evenings. Before hiring an instructor for a beginner course, it asked which weeknight people could attend. Of 23 replies, 14 picked Tuesday, 6 picked Thursday, and 3 picked Wednesday. The course goes on the spring schedule for Tuesdays.
fields.tab_content_2:
U14 sits four players short of a team

Pine Hollow Youth Lacrosse sets its teams from a player interest form that opens in January. Parents enter the player's age group and position. The club needs 15 players to field a team. The U14 group has 11, and the form flagged it so the board can recruit four more before tryouts.
fields.tab_content_3:
Two-bedroom prices reach the 41 who asked

Marlow Yards opens in March, and its leasing team started an interest list before the drywall went up. Renters pick a floor plan and a move-in month. When two-bedroom prices were set, the app emailed them to the 41 people who chose two bedrooms. The leasing channel in Slack got the count.
fields.tab_content_4:
No mentor yet for three forecasting mentees

Brightwater Logistics is starting a mentoring program for planners. Employees choose mentor or mentee and pick a skill. Each mentee is paired with a mentor who chose the same skill. Five asked for forecasting and two mentors offered it. HR got the three unmatched names.

fields.howto_title: How to Make an Interest Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to make an interest form that settles one decision with a clear go-ahead number, then build it with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Set the number that makes it a go
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write down what the replies decide: which night to run a course, whether an age group fields a team, how many mentors to recruit. If no answer to a question would change your plan, it belongs on a later form.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Pick your threshold before the form opens: 15 players for a team, say, or 12 sign-ups for a class night. Deciding first keeps you honest when replies land a little under the line, and it tells the app when to alert you.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Beyond contact details, ask only the two or three answers that drive the decision, such as preferred night. Put an optional comment box last. Each extra required field loses people who were only mildly curious.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Tell people on the form when they will hear back, for example by March 1. Add a checkbox for updates by email. A stated date keeps a quiet month from looking like a dead project, and it gives you a deadline too.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Paste the questions and the threshold into one prompt, and name who gets alerted. Emergent builds the form, a database of replies, and a dashboard with a count per option. Change any part later by asking, such as lowering the threshold to 10.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Draft the message people get when the plan is confirmed, and choose who receives it by their answers. Players get the tryout date for their own age group. Send it with one click or schedule it for the day you announce.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Submit the form twice with the same email and confirm the second reply updates your row instead of adding one. Check that the dashboard count moves and that a test alert arrives. Clear the test rows, then share the link.

plan.angle: The live top 10 is template pages (Woorise, Typeform volunteer interest, Jotform, Snapforms registration of interest, Fomr student interest), a Google Forms help article and two live forms. Each one stops at the fields: name, email, a checkbox of interests. None shows what an interest form is for, which is a decision made before anything is scheduled or built: which night to run a class, whether an age group fields a team, who hears first when prices are out, how many mentors to recruit. This page answers the expression-of-interest questions searchers ask, then shows four organizers turning responses into that decision, with a tally, a roster rule, a targeted release email and a match by skill.
tab_stories: Fernhill Community College wants to run an evening woodworking course and asks which weeknight people could attend, and Tuesday draws 14 of the 23 replies, which sets the night.
Pine Hollow Youth Lacrosse collects player interest by age group before the season, and its rule flags the U14 group at 11 players, four short of the 15 it needs to field a team.

Marlow Yards, an apartment building opening in March, collects floor plan and move-in month from prospective renters, and when two-bedroom prices are released only the 41 people who chose two bedrooms get the email.

Brightwater Logistics opens a workplace mentoring program where employees say whether they want to mentor or be mentored and pick one skill, and three mentees who chose forecasting are left without a mentor, so HR gets that gap to recruit for.

scope.evidence: H1 'Build an Interest Form That Counts Demand Before You Commit' and hero 'tells you when demand clears your bar' cover the primary, not sign up form or lead capture form.

intent.evidence: Tool intent led by Google Forms: the page is a builder, the table compares Google Forms, Jotform and Typeform, and the FAQ covers both PAA questions (definition, expression of interest) plus template and PDF.

specificity.evidence: Demand-measuring vocabulary: 'the number that makes it worth it', '15 players to field a team', 'Two-bedroom prices reach the 41 who asked', 'Totals count people, not submissions'.

openers.evidence: Full-sentence openers: 'Show the skill-level question only to people who pick the beginner course', 'Write down what the replies decide', 'Pick your threshold before the form opens'.

voice.evidence: Operator details: 'a woodshop that sits empty most evenings', 'before the drywall went up', 'A stated date keeps a quiet month from looking like a dead project'.

truth.evidence: Expression of interest before a formal application matches the Law Insider source; Emergent claims map to prompt-build, database-owned, alerts, code-export; numbers agree (14 + 6 + 3 = 23, 15 - 11 = 4, 5 - 2 = 3).

distinct.evidence: Tabs (evening class, youth lacrosse, apartment pre-leasing, mentoring) are distinct; FAQ 7 separates interest form from sign up form and links it rather than covering it.

faq.evidence: 10 on-topic questions, answer-first; hub link in item 2; links to creator application, sign up form and registration form.

images.evidence: Tab 1 'Tuesday: 14 of 23 replies'; tab 2 'U14 has 11 players / 4 short of a team'; tab 3 'Emailed to 41 prospects'; tab 4 '5 asked, 2 mentors offered' / '3 mentees unmatched' match the copy.
